intent.raw_query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Leap from New Zealand's highest bungy platform at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience offers a 8.5-second freefall with breathtaking views of the surrounding Remarkables mountain range. Includes transport from Queenstown and a commemorative certificate.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike one of New Zealand's nine Great Walks, a stunning 32km trail through Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks. Trek past alpine lakes, ancient beech forests, and dramatic mountain passes with panoramic views. A multi-day hike best done over 2-3 days with DOC hut stays along the route.

experiences.name: Hooker Valley Track to Mueller Glacier
experiences.description: Walk one of the most accessible yet spectacular hikes in Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park. This 10km return trail crosses three swing bridges and leads to a glacial lake filled with icebergs at the foot of New Zealand's highest peak. The dramatic alpine scenery is unmatched on the South Island.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo
experiences.description: Paddle through the dramatic fiords of Milford Sound at dawn before the tour boats arrive, gliding past Mitre Peak and cascading waterfalls. Combine with a guided walk on the Milford foreshore track to experience the lush rainforest, resident seals, and dolphins in their natural habitat.

experiences.name: Abel Tasman Coast Track Hiking and Beach Exploration
experiences.description: Hike sections of the famous Abel Tasman Coast Track, weaving through golden beaches, turquoise bays, and native bush. Take a water taxi to drop off and hike back through Torrent Bay and Anchorage, swimming at pristine beaches along the way. A perfect blend of hiking and coastal beauty unique to the South Island.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - New Zealand South Island
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

The dramatic alpine scenery is unmatched on the South Island.

experiences.name: Abel Tasman Coast Track Hiking and Beach Exploration

Take a water taxi to drop off and hike back through Torrent Bay and Anchorage, swimming at pristine beaches along the way. A perfect blend of hiking and coastal beauty unique to the South Island.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Queenstown Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and recover from flight.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, collect luggage and take the Orbus public bus (Line 1, ~NZD $2) from the airport to Queenstown town centre. Check in to Nevis Valley, Queenstown Boutique Stay. Take a relaxed orientation walk along the Queenstown lakefront and Earnslaw Wharf to get your bearings. Enjoy views of The Remarkables mountain range — completely free.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Queenstown Night Market on Beach Street (open Sundays, ~NZD $10–15 for street food). Browse local food stalls for budget-friendly bites like hangi pork, fresh crepes, and hot chips.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the plane or grab a snack at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Fergburger on Shotover Street — iconic Queenstown burger joint, budget-friendly at ~NZD $12–16 per burger.
meals.dinner: Queenstown Night Market on Beach Street — mix of street food stalls, budget ~NZD $10–15 for a full meal.

day_by_day.notes: Day 1 is purely arrival and orientation. No strenuous activities. Pick up a free Queenstown visitor map from the i-SITE information centre near the lakefront. Buy a local SIM card at the airport (2degrees or Skinny Mobile, ~NZD $20 with data) for navigation throughout the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning hike up the Ben Lomond Track starting point via the Tiki Trail from Queenstown town centre. Hike to the Ben Lomond Saddle (approximately 3–4 hours return to saddle, free entry). Stunning panoramic views of Lake Wakatipu and The Remarkables. Bring packed snacks and water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend back to town and visit the free Queenstown Gardens for a relaxed afternoon stroll. Explore the rose garden, frisbee golf course, and lakeside paths. Rest your legs and enjoy the scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Queenstown waterfront at sunset — golden hour views over Lake Wakatipu are spectacular and free. Head back to the accommodation to prepare gear for upcoming activities.

meals.breakfast: Self-cater at accommodation — buy supplies from Countdown Supermarket on Gorge Road (~NZD $5–8 for oats, fruit, bread).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from supermarket supplies eaten at the Ben Lomond Saddle — sandwiches, muesli bars, fruit (~NZD $5).
meals.dinner: Vudu Cafe & Larder on Rees Street — hearty, wholesome meals with vegetarian options, budget ~NZD $18–22 per main.

day_by_day.notes: The Ben Lomond Saddle hike is free and one of the best views in Queenstown. Wear sturdy shoes and sunscreen. November weather can be warm but changeable — pack a light rain layer. The full summit adds another 2 hours; attempt only if energy permits.

day_by_day.morning: Nevis Bungy Jump — book in advance through AJ Hackett Bungy (Nevis Bungy, 134m, the highest in New Zealand, ~NZD $275). Transfer departs from Queenstown town centre at 8:00am to the Nevis Valley site (approximately 45 minutes). This is a bucket-list experience and the centrepiece of the trip given the accommodation location near Nevis Valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return transfer to Queenstown arrives around 1:00pm. Decompress with a relaxed lunch. Visit the free Kiwi Birdlife Park entrance area or walk along the Queenstown Hill Time Walk (free, 2 hours return) for gentle post-adrenaline exercise with great town views.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the bungy jump with a budget dinner out. Walk the lakefront at dusk and enjoy the buzz of Queenstown's evening atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast at accommodation before the 8:00am transfer — toast, peanut butter, banana (~NZD $3).
meals.lunch: Devil Burger on The Mall — affordable gourmet burgers ~NZD $13–16, great post-bungy refuel.
meals.dinner: Eichardt's Public Bar on Marine Parade — pub-style meals, fish and chips or schnitzel ~NZD $18–24.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Nevis Bungy well in advance as it sells out quickly in November (peak season). AJ Hackett offers combo deals — check their website for discounts if combining with other activities. The Nevis Bungy includes a gondola-style cable car to the suspended pod above the Nevis River gorge. Minimum weight 45kg, maximum 127kg. Photos and video packages available at extra cost (~NZD $50–80) — consider splitting cost with travel companions.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or take a bus to Glenorchy (45 minutes from Queenstown, free scenic road along Lake Wakatipu). Walk the Glenorchy Lagoon Boardwalk (free, 1 hour easy loop) through wetlands with views of snow-capped mountains. This area was used as a filming location for Lord of the Rings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Routeburn Track Day Walk from Glenorchy — hike to Routeburn Flats (approximately 4 hours return, free). Stunning beech forest, mountain views, and river crossings. Pack plenty of water and snacks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown by late afternoon. Rest at accommodation and do laundry if needed. Low-key evening to recover from the week's activities.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — muesli, yoghurt, coffee (~NZD $4).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch taken to Glenorchy — supermarket sandwiches, fruit, trail mix (~NZD $6).
meals.dinner: Countdown Supermarket — buy ingredients and cook a simple pasta or rice meal at accommodation (~NZD $8–10). Great budget saver.

day_by_day.notes: The drive to Glenorchy is one of the most scenic in New Zealand — stop at multiple viewpoints along the way. If you don't have a rental car, the Glenorchy Air shuttle runs day trips from Queenstown (~NZD $25 return). Check the DOC (Department of Conservation) website for current track conditions before heading out. November can bring afternoon thunderstorms in the mountains — start hikes early.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Queenstown early by rental car or InterCity bus toward Wanaka (~1 hour drive). Check out of Nevis Valley accommodation. On arrival in Wanaka, hike the Mount Iron Track (1.5 hours return, free) — a short but rewarding hike with 360-degree views of Lake Wanaka and surrounding mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk along the Wanaka lakefront and visit the famous 'That Wanaka Tree' — the lone willow tree growing in the lake, an iconic New Zealand photo spot (free). Explore the town centre and browse local shops. Visit Puzzling World (~NZD $16 entry) if budget allows — a quirky attraction with illusion rooms and a giant maze.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into budget accommodation in Wanaka (book Wanaka Bakpaka or Base Wanaka hostel, dorm ~NZD $30–40/night). Enjoy the relaxed Wanaka vibe.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast at Queenstown accommodation before departure.
meals.lunch: Kai Whakapai Cafe on the Wanaka lakefront — great sandwiches and cabinet food ~NZD $10–14.
meals.dinner: Francesca's Italian Kitchen on Helwick Street — wood-fired pizza and pasta, generous portions ~NZD $18–22.

day_by_day.notes: InterCity buses run Queenstown to Wanaka daily — check timetables and book ahead (~NZD $15–25). If renting a car, the Crown Range Road (State Highway 89) offers a spectacular alternative route with panoramic views — allow extra time. Wanaka is a more relaxed and slightly cheaper town than Queenstown. Stock up at New World Supermarket in Wanaka for self-catering supplies.

day_by_day.morning: Rob Roy Glacier Track — one of the best day hikes in New Zealand (10km return, 3–4 hours, free). Drive 55km from Wanaka to the Raspberry Creek car park (4WD recommended for river crossing, or park before the crossing). Hike through beech forest to a stunning hanging glacier and waterfall viewpoint. Start early to avoid afternoon crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the Rob Roy hike by early afternoon. Stop at the Blue Pools on the Makarora River on the way back (~30 minutes detour, free DOC walk, 1 hour return). Crystal-clear blue water with a swing bridge — great for photos.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Wanaka. Relax sore muscles with a lakeside sunset stroll. Explore Wanaka's small but lively bar scene.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast at hostel — packed and ready before 7:30am departure.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at the Rob Roy Glacier viewpoint — sandwiches, energy bars, fruit (~NZD $6). There are no facilities on the track.
meals.dinner: Ritual Cafe on Ardmore Street, Wanaka — affordable breakfast-all-day and dinner menu ~NZD $15–20.

day_by_day.notes: The Rob Roy Glacier Track requires a river crossing at Raspberry Creek which can be impassable after heavy rain — check DOC conditions the night before. Wear waterproof hiking boots. The track gains 400m elevation — allow extra time if not accustomed to hill hiking. November days are long (sunset ~9pm) giving plenty of daylight. Carry at least 2 litres of water per person.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Wanaka and drive south toward Te Anau (~3 hours via State Highway 6 and 94). Scenic drive through the Lindis Pass with sweeping tussock landscapes. Stop at Cromwell for a quick walk through the Old Cromwell Town historic precinct (free) and grab fresh stone fruit from a local roadside stall (~NZD $5).
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Te Anau by early afternoon. Check in to Te Anau YHA or Barnyard Backpackers (dorm ~NZD $30–38/night). Walk the Te Anau lakefront track (free, 2km easy walk) along the shores of Lake Te Anau — the second largest lake in New Zealand.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the DOC Te Anau visitor centre (free) to plan the Milford Sound day trip and get current track conditions for upcoming hikes. Explore the small Te Anau town centre.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Wanaka hostel before departure.
meals.lunch: Roadside stop in Cromwell — fresh fruit from the Cromwell Fruit Stalls and a pie from a local bakery (~NZD $8).
meals.dinner: The Sandfly Cafe on The Lane, Te Anau — local favourite, affordable burgers and wraps ~NZD $14–18.

day_by_day.notes: Fill up your rental car with petrol in Wanaka or Cromwell — fuel is significantly more expensive in Te Anau and there are no petrol stations between Te Anau and Milford Sound. Buy groceries at the Four Square supermarket in Te Anau for the next two days of packed lunches. November is the start of the busy Fiordland season — book Milford Sound tours in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Te Anau at 7:00am for the 2-hour drive to Milford Sound along the stunning Milford Road (State Highway 94). Stop at Mirror Lakes (free, 10-minute walk), The Chasm walk (free, 20-minute loop), and the Homer Tunnel. Arrive at Milford Sound by 9:30am.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a budget Milford Sound cruise — Real Journeys or Go Orange offer scenic cruises from ~NZD $45–65 per person (book online in advance for best prices). The 1.5-hour cruise takes you past Mitre Peak, Stirling Falls, and Bowen Falls with possible dolphin and seal sightings. After the cruise, walk the short Foreshore Walk at Milford (~30 minutes, free).
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Te Anau, arriving around 6:00pm. The return drive at golden hour is equally spectacular. Rest and prepare gear for the next day's hike.

meals.breakfast: Very early self-catered breakfast at Te Anau hostel — porridge and coffee before 7:00am departure.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Milford Sound — there is a small cafe at the terminal but it is overpriced. Bring your own food from Te Anau supermarket (~NZD $6).
meals.dinner: Ristorante Pizzeria Paradiso on Town Centre, Te Anau — wood-fired pizza ~NZD $18–22, great value.

day_by_day.notes: The Milford Road is one of the most scenic drives in the world — allow extra time for stops. Check for road closures or avalanche warnings in November (check NZTA website the night before). Book the Milford Sound cruise well in advance for November travel. The cruise is weather-dependent but runs in rain — Milford actually looks dramatic in wet weather. Sandflies are fierce at Milford — bring insect repellent.

day_by_day.morning: Kepler Track Day Hike — depart Te Anau early for the Kepler Track Control Gates (10-minute drive or 1-hour walk from town). Hike to the Luxmore Hut (approximately 5–6 hours return, free day use). The track climbs through beech forest to the alpine zone with stunning views over Lake Te Anau and the Fiordland mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue along the ridge toward Luxmore Hut if energy allows, or begin descent after reaching the treeline viewpoints. The alpine section above the treeline offers some of the best panoramic views in Fiordland.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Te Anau by late afternoon. Soak tired feet and relax. Pack bags for tomorrow's departure toward the West Coast.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast at hostel — eggs on toast, coffee (~NZD $4).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the Kepler Track — substantial food needed for the climb: wraps, cheese, nuts, chocolate (~NZD $7).
meals.dinner: Miles Better Pies on Town Centre, Te Anau — excellent pies and hot food, budget ~NZD $8–12. Great value.

day_by_day.notes: The Kepler Track to Luxmore Hut is a significant climb gaining approximately 900m elevation. Start no later than 8:00am to allow sufficient time. The DOC hut fee is not required for day walkers. Check weather forecast — the exposed alpine ridge section should not be attempted in high winds or thunderstorm conditions. November can bring unpredictable weather in Fiordland — always carry a rain jacket and extra layers.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Te Anau and drive north toward the West Coast via State Highway 94 and 6 (approximately 4–5 hours to Franz Josef Glacier area). Scenic drive through Haast Pass — stop at Thunder Creek Falls (free, 10-minute return walk from the road) and the Gates of Haast Bridge viewpoint.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue north along the West Coast. Stop at Knights Point Lookout (free) for spectacular ocean views. Arrive in Franz Josef township by late afternoon. Check in to budget accommodation — Franz Josef YHA or Rainforest Retreat (dorm ~NZD $32–42/night).
day_by_day.evening: Walk the short Sentinel Rock Walk in Franz Josef (free, 20 minutes) for views toward the glacier valley at golden hour. Explore the small township.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Te Anau hostel before departure.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at a scenic stop along the Haast Pass — roadside picnic area near Thunder Creek Falls (~NZD $6).
meals.dinner: The Landing Bar and Restaurant in Franz Josef — pub meals, burgers and fish and chips ~NZD $16–22.

day_by_day.notes: The Haast Pass drive is approximately 330km from Te Anau to Franz Josef — fill up with fuel in Haast township (the only petrol station for a long stretch). The West Coast road can be affected by flooding and slips in November — check NZTA for road conditions. Franz Josef township is small with limited supermarket options — the Four Square is expensive. Stock up on supplies in Wanaka or Te Anau if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Franz Josef Glacier Valley Walk — hike the free glacier valley walk to the glacier viewpoint (approximately 2.5 hours return, free). The track follows the Waiho River through the glacier valley to a viewing platform with close-up views of the Franz Josef Glacier ice face. Note: the glacier has retreated significantly but the valley scenery is still stunning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive 25km south to Fox Glacier and walk the Fox Glacier Valley Track (free, 2 hours return) to the glacier terminal viewpoint. The twin glacier experience in one day is unique to this part of New Zealand. Stop at Lake Matheson (free, 1.5-hour loop walk) for the famous 'Mirror Lake' reflection of Aoraki/Mount Cook and Mount Tasman.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Franz Josef. Relax and rest for the big drive and hike tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at hostel — porridge, coffee, fruit (~NZD $4).
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Lake Matheson picnic area — sandwiches and snacks from Four Square (~NZD $7).
meals.dinner: Speight's Ale House in Franz Josef — hearty pub meals, good value at ~NZD $18–22.

day_by_day.notes: Both glacier valley walks are free DOC tracks. Guided glacier hikes are available but expensive (~NZD $160–200) — the free valley walks still offer impressive views. Lake Matheson is best visited in the early morning for perfect reflections (calm wind conditions), but the afternoon visit is still worthwhile. The Westland Tai Poutini National Park visitor centre in Franz Josef has excellent free exhibits on glacier formation.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Franz Josef early and drive east through Arthur's Pass toward Christchurch (approximately 4–5 hours). Stop at Arthur's Pass National Park — hike the Devils Punchbowl Waterfall Track (free, 1 hour return) to a stunning 131m waterfall. The alpine village of Arthur's Pass has a DOC visitor centre worth a quick stop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving to Christchurch, arriving by early afternoon (~2.5 hours from Arthur's Pass). Check in to budget accommodation — Jucy Snooze Christchurch or Base Christchurch hostel (dorm ~NZD $28–38/night). Explore the Christchurch Botanic Gardens (free entry, 75 hectares of beautiful gardens along the Avon River).
day_by_day.evening: Walk through the Christchurch city centre and visit the Re:START Container Mall and the Cardboard Cathedral — fascinating examples of the city's post-earthquake rebuild. The city centre at night is vibrant with street art and murals.

meals.breakfast: Very early self-catered breakfast at Franz Josef hostel before departure.
meals.lunch: Stop at the Arthur's Pass Bakery and Cafe in the village — pies, sandwiches ~NZD $8–12.
meals.dinner: Pomeroy's Old Brewery Inn on Kilmore Street, Christchurch — excellent craft beer and pub food ~NZD $16–22.

day_by_day.notes: The Arthur's Pass to Christchurch drive through the Canterbury Plains is a dramatic change of scenery from the West Coast — vast flat farmland after days of mountains. The TranzAlpine train is a famous scenic option between Greymouth and Christchurch (~NZD $109–149) but requires leaving your rental car — not practical for this itinerary. Christchurch has excellent free attractions — download the Christchurch Street Art map app.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Christchurch — visit the free Canterbury Museum on Rolleston Avenue (excellent natural history and Māori taonga collections). Walk along the Avon River Precinct (Otākaro Avon River Corridor) — a beautiful free riverside walk through the heart of the city with public art installations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Christchurch Botanic Gardens Peacock Fountain area and take a free walk through the native plant collection. If time permits, visit the free Christchurch Art Gallery Te Puna o Waiwhetū on Worcester Boulevard — one of New Zealand's premier public art galleries. Head to the airport for departure (allow 2 hours before flight).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Christchurch International Airport. Reflect on 13 incredible days of hiking, bungy jumping, glaciers, fiords, and South Island adventures.

meals.breakfast: C1 Espresso on High Street — famous Christchurch cafe, great breakfast options ~NZD $12–16.
meals.lunch: Riverside Market on Oxford Terrace — food hall with diverse affordable options ~NZD $10–15. Great final South Island meal.
meals.dinner: Airport meal or in-flight depending on departure time — budget ~NZD $15–20 for airport food.

day_by_day.notes: Return the rental car at Christchurch Airport if applicable — allow extra time for the return process (30–45 minutes). Christchurch Airport is compact and easy to navigate. The free Orbis bus route runs from the city centre to the airport. Do a final check of accommodation and transport to ensure nothing is left behind. Consider buying New Zealand souvenirs at the Riverside Market rather than the airport for better prices. The South Island trip covers approximately 2,000km of driving if using a rental car throughout.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Land at Queenstown Airport at 13:00. Collect luggage, pick up rental car, and drive to Nevis Valley, Queenstown Boutique Stay (~45 min). Check in, freshen up, and take a relaxed orientation walk around the Queenstown waterfront and town centre to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Queenstown's vibrant lakefront. Walk along Lake Wakatipu, browse the town centre, and enjoy your first New Zealand dinner.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the flight or grab a snack at Queenstown Airport café upon arrival
meals.lunch: Grab a casual bite near the airport or en route — try a local pie from a bakery or a quick café stop in Frankton
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant on The Mall — mid-range, locally sourced New Zealand cuisine with a relaxed atmosphere perfect for a first night

day_by_day.notes: Nothing is scheduled before arrival. Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Confirm rental car booking and stock up on groceries or snacks for the coming days at a Queenstown supermarket (Countdown or New World on Gorge Road).

day_by_day.morning: NEVIS BUNGY JUMP — Head to the AJ Hackett Nevis Bungy base in Queenstown town centre for your 9:00 AM check-in. Transfer by 4WD bus to the Nevis River gorge platform. Leap from New Zealand's highest bungy at 134 meters above the Nevis River — an 8.5-second freefall and a truly iconic adrenaline experience. Allow 3–4 hours for the full experience including transfers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown by early afternoon. Decompress and celebrate with a leisurely stroll along the Queenstown Bay boardwalk. Visit Bob's Peak via the Skyline Gondola for panoramic views over Lake Wakatipu and The Remarkables mountain range.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy sunset views from the Skyline complex or head back into town for dinner along the waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Eat a light breakfast at the hotel or grab something at a Queenstown café before heading to the Nevis base — try Vudu Café on Rees Street for great coffee and eggs
meals.lunch: Post-bungy celebration lunch at Fergburger on Shotover Street — a Queenstown institution, famous for generous gourmet burgers
meals.dinner: Pub dinner at The Cow Restaurant — cozy stone-walled spot known for pizza and pasta, great mid-range value

day_by_day.notes: Book Nevis Bungy well in advance through AJ Hackett. Wear comfortable, secure clothing and closed-toe shoes. Minimum weight 45kg, maximum 127kg. The experience includes a certificate and optional jump video/photos for purchase. Arrive well-rested and avoid a heavy breakfast beforehand.

day_by_day.morning: Drive from Queenstown toward Glenorchy (~45 min along the scenic Glenorchy Road hugging Lake Wakatipu). Stop at multiple viewpoints along the way. Arrive in Glenorchy and begin the start of the ROUTEBURN TRACK — hike the first section from the Glenorchy end (Routeburn Shelter to Routeburn Flats, ~2 hours one way, 8km return). Enjoy the beech forest and river valley scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue deeper on the track to Routeburn Falls Hut (~4 hours return from shelter) if energy permits, or turn back at the Flats. Have a picnic lunch at the river flats. Return to the car park and drive back toward Queenstown.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown. Rest and recover from the day's hiking.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel — pack a lunch the night before
meals.lunch: Packed picnic lunch eaten on the Routeburn Flats by the river — sandwiches, fruit, trail mix, and a thermos of coffee
meals.dinner: Fishbone Bar & Grill in Queenstown — excellent mid-range seafood and New Zealand lamb dishes

day_by_day.notes: This day covers the accessible day-hike portion of the Routeburn Track without requiring hut bookings. If you wish to do the full 32km Great Walk over 2–3 days with hut stays, book DOC huts well in advance (they open for booking in June for the season). Weather can change rapidly — bring a rain jacket, layers, and sturdy hiking boots. November is early summer so conditions are generally good but be prepared.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day in Queenstown. Sleep in and enjoy a slow morning. Visit the Queenstown Gardens — a peaceful lakeside park great for a gentle morning walk. Explore the rose garden and disc golf course.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a jet boat ride on the Shotover River (Shotover Jet — a classic Queenstown activity, ~1 hour) for an exhilarating but less physically demanding adventure. Alternatively, visit the Kiwi Birdlife Park for a cultural and wildlife experience.
day_by_day.evening: Wander the Queenstown Night Market (runs Thursday–Sunday on the Beach Street waterfront) or explore the town's boutique shops and galleries.

meals.breakfast: Lazy brunch at Bespoke Kitchen on Isle Street — excellent healthy café with great eggs, smoothie bowls, and coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a waterfront café — try Yonder on Rees Street for a relaxed mid-range menu
meals.dinner: Flame Bar & Grill on The Mall — New Zealand beef and lamb, mid-range steakhouse with good atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: Use this day to do laundry, restock supplies, and plan logistics for the upcoming multi-day drives. Book any remaining activities if not already confirmed. Check weather forecasts for the Milford Sound and Mount Cook sections coming up.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Queenstown early (~7:00 AM) and drive toward Te Anau (~2.5 hours via SH6). Check in to accommodation in Te Anau — the gateway to Fiordland. Visit the DOC Fiordland National Park Visitor Centre to learn about the park and confirm Milford Sound plans.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Te Anau township and Lake Te Anau. Take a short hike on the Kepler Track day-walk section — the Control Gates to the Rocky Point lookout (~2 hours return, flat and easy) is a beautiful lakeside walk through beech forest.
day_by_day.evening: Relax in Te Anau and prepare gear for the big Milford Sound day tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departing Queenstown
meals.lunch: Stop in Mossburn or Five Rivers on the drive — packed lunch or a roadside café
meals.dinner: Redcliff Restaurant in Te Anau — charming mid-range restaurant with great New Zealand cuisine in a historic cottage setting

day_by_day.notes: Te Anau is a small town — book accommodation in advance. The drive from Queenstown to Te Anau is scenic and straightforward. Fill up your rental car with petrol in Te Anau as there are no fuel stops on the Milford Road. Pack rain gear — Fiordland receives heavy rainfall year-round, which actually makes the waterfalls more spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: MILFORD SOUND KAYAK AND HIKE COMBO — Depart Te Anau at 5:30 AM for the 2-hour drive along the spectacular Milford Road (SH94). Arrive at Milford Sound by 7:30 AM for your dawn kayaking session. Paddle through the dramatic fiords before the tour boats arrive — glide past Mitre Peak, beneath Stirling Falls, and along towering cliff faces. The early morning light and mist on the water is truly magical.
day_by_day.afternoon: After kayaking, join the guided hike component of the combo — explore the rainforest trails around the Milford Sound foreshore and Cleddau Valley. Take in the Homer Tunnel and Chasm Walk on the return drive to Te Anau.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Te Anau by early evening. Hot shower and a well-earned dinner.

meals.breakfast: Very early light breakfast or snacks before departure — pack energy bars and a thermos of coffee for the drive
meals.lunch: Pack a substantial lunch to eat at Milford Sound — the café at Milford Sound Lodge is an option but can be expensive; packed lunch recommended
meals.dinner: Miles Better Pies or The Fat Duck in Te Anau — casual, hearty, and mid-range; perfect for a tired evening

day_by_day.notes: Book the Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo well in advance — Rosco's Milford Kayaks is a reputable operator. The Milford Road is one of the world's most scenic drives — allow extra time for stops at Mirror Lakes, Lake Gunn, and the Chasm. Check avalanche and road conditions before departure (especially in November when snowmelt can cause slips). Bring waterproof gear, sunscreen, and insect repellent (sandflies are notorious at Milford).

day_by_day.morning: Depart Te Anau and drive north toward Lake Pukaki and Aoraki/Mount Cook (~4.5 hours via SH8 through Twizel). Stop at Tekapo for a short break — visit the Church of the Good Shepherd on the lake shore and enjoy the turquoise glacial waters of Lake Tekapo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Twizel and then drive the Mount Cook Road to Aoraki/Mount Cook Village (~1 hour from Twizel). Check in to accommodation at The Hermitage or similar. Take the short Kea Point Track (~2 hours return) for your first views of Aoraki/Mount Cook and the Mueller Glacier terminal lake.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the extraordinary dark sky stargazing at Mount Cook — the Mackenzie Basin is one of the world's top stargazing locations (International Dark Sky Reserve). Join a guided stargazing tour if available.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Te Anau accommodation before departing
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Lake Tekapo — pick up supplies at a Tekapo superette or café
meals.dinner: The Old Mountaineers Café & Bar at Mount Cook Village — mid-range, great atmosphere with views of the mountains, good burgers and New Zealand fare

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Te Anau to Mount Cook is long but stunning — allow a full day. Mount Cook Village has limited dining options so book dinner in advance if possible. November weather at Mount Cook can be unpredictable — temperatures drop significantly at altitude even in summer. Bring warm layers, waterproofs, and sunscreen (UV is intense at altitude). The Mackenzie Basin stargazing is world-class — Dark Sky Project in Tekapo offers excellent tours.

day_by_day.morning: HOOKER VALLEY TRACK TO MUELLER GLACIER — Begin the hike early (7:00–8:00 AM) to beat the crowds. This spectacular 10km return trail crosses three swing bridges over the Hooker River, passes the Mueller Glacier terminal lake, and culminates at the Hooker Lake at the foot of Aoraki/Mount Cook with dramatic floating icebergs. Allow 3–4 hours return.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the village by midday. Rest, have lunch, and if energy allows, take the Tasman Glacier View Track (~1.5 hours return) for views over New Zealand's longest glacier.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the accommodation. Enjoy the alpenglow on Aoraki/Mount Cook at sunset — the mountain turns extraordinary shades of pink and orange.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before heading to the trailhead — pack snacks and water for the hike
meals.lunch: Post-hike lunch at The Old Mountaineers Café — hearty sandwiches, soup, and coffee
meals.dinner: Panorama Restaurant at The Hermitage — slightly more upscale but worth it for the occasion; stunning mountain views and a good New Zealand menu at reasonable prices

day_by_day.notes: The Hooker Valley Track is one of the most iconic and accessible hikes in New Zealand — do not miss it. Start early to avoid tour groups. The swing bridges are fun but may be challenging for those with a strong fear of heights. The icebergs in Hooker Lake are a highlight — bring a camera with a good zoom lens. Weather can change rapidly — check the DOC forecast and turn back if conditions deteriorate. Sunscreen and sunglasses are essential.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Mount Cook Village and drive north to Nelson/Abel Tasman region (~5–6 hours via SH1 through Christchurch or SH8 to Fairlie and SH1 north). This is a long driving day — depart by 7:00 AM. Stop in Christchurch for lunch and a brief exploration of the city's remarkable post-earthquake regeneration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving north through Kaikōura (stop for a quick coastal walk and possible whale/dolphin sighting from the shore) toward Nelson. Arrive in Motueka or Nelson by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Check in to accommodation near Motueka (gateway to Abel Tasman National Park). Settle in and relax after a long driving day.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Mount Cook accommodation before departing
meals.lunch: Lunch in Christchurch — try Harlequin Public House or a café in the Riverside Market for good mid-range options
meals.dinner: The Mussel Inn at Onekaka (if passing through Golden Bay route) or a local restaurant in Motueka — try Precinct on High or a local pizza spot

day_by_day.notes: This is the longest driving day of the trip (~5–6 hours). Consider breaking it into two days if you prefer a more relaxed pace — Kaikōura makes an excellent overnight stop with whale watching tours available. If driving straight through, take regular breaks, share driving if possible, and be alert for SH1 traffic. Book Motueka/Abel Tasman accommodation well in advance as it fills up in November (peak season).

day_by_day.morning: ABEL TASMAN COAST TRACK — Depart Motueka early and drive to Marahau (30 min), the southern entrance to Abel Tasman National Park. Begin hiking the Abel Tasman Coast Track heading north. The first section from Marahau to Anchorage (~3 hours one way, 11km) winds through golden beaches, turquoise bays, and native forest. Swim at Coquille Bay or Stillwell Bay en route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach Anchorage Beach — one of the most beautiful beaches in New Zealand. Swim, relax, and explore. Take the optional side trail to the Anchorage headland for panoramic views. Return to Marahau via water taxi (book in advance with Abel Tasman Aquataxi) for a different perspective — gliding past seal colonies and sea caves.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Motueka. Shower and enjoy a relaxed evening.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast in Motueka before heading to the park — pack a full day's food and water
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten on Anchorage Beach — this is a highlight of the trip, dining on one of NZ's most beautiful beaches
meals.dinner: Jester House Café in Motueka (open for dinner in summer) or The Smoking Barrel — relaxed mid-range dining with good local produce

day_by_day.notes: Book water taxi return from Anchorage in advance — Abel Tasman Aquataxi and other operators run regular services. The water taxi adds a wonderful dimension to the day. Bring plenty of water (3+ litres per person), sunscreen, insect repellent (sandflies), a swimsuit, and a dry bag for your belongings. November is peak season — the track can be busy but the weather is excellent. Tides affect some beach crossings — check tide tables with DOC or your water taxi operator.

day_by_day.morning: Explore more of the Abel Tasman Coast Track — hike the section from Torrent Bay to Bark Bay (~4km, 1.5 hours) or do a longer section toward Tonga Island Marine Reserve. The Tonga Island area offers excellent snorkeling and a seal colony viewpoint. Alternatively, hire a sea kayak from Marahau for a half-day paddle along the coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive from Motueka to Nelson (~1 hour). Explore Nelson city — visit the Nelson Market (Saturday/Sunday) or browse the arts and crafts galleries that Nelson is famous for. Walk up to the Centre of New Zealand viewpoint for panoramic views over the city and Tasman Bay.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Nelson's excellent dining and craft beer scene — Nelson is known as the craft beer capital of New Zealand.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at Motueka accommodation or a café in Motueka town
meals.lunch: Pack a lunch for the morning hike or kayak, eaten on the beach
meals.dinner: Hopgoods & Co in Nelson — excellent mid-range restaurant with local produce and a great wine list; or The Free House craft beer pub for a more casual evening with excellent local beers

day_by_day.notes: Sea kayaking in Abel Tasman is a wonderful experience — operators like Kaiteriteri Kayaks offer half-day guided tours. Nelson is a vibrant small city with a strong arts scene — the World of WearableArt museum is worth a visit if time allows. This is a good day to do laundry and repack for the final days of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a relaxed final full morning in Nelson. Visit the Nelson Saturday Market if applicable, or explore Founders Heritage Park. Take a gentle walk along the Maitai River Valley Track (2–3 hours return from the city centre) through native bush — a lovely easy hike right from the city.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive from Nelson back toward Queenstown or to Christchurch for the return flight (depending on departure logistics). Nelson to Christchurch is ~4.5 hours via SH6 and SH1 (Lewis Pass route) — a scenic drive through the Southern Alps. Alternatively, fly Nelson to Christchurch (30 min) if budget allows.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Christchurch. Check in to accommodation and explore the city's innovative post-earthquake regeneration — the Cardboard Cathedral, the Container Mall, and the Avon River precinct are fascinating.

meals.breakfast: Final Nelson breakfast at a local café — try Lambretta's Café & Bar for excellent coffee and brunch
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or stop at Hanmer Springs (if taking the Lewis Pass route) for a quick bite and optional hot pools dip
meals.dinner: Christchurch dinner at Inati Restaurant on Lichfield Street — excellent mid-range contemporary New Zealand cuisine in the heart of the rebuilt city

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure flight details and whether you are flying home from Christchurch or Queenstown — adjust this day's driving accordingly. If flying from Queenstown, the drive from Nelson to Queenstown is ~6 hours and may require an overnight stop in Christchurch or Wanaka. Return the rental car at the correct airport. Christchurch is a fascinating city that has reinvented itself after the 2011 earthquake — worth at least an evening's exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in New Zealand. If in Christchurch, visit the Botanic Gardens for a peaceful farewell walk — one of the finest botanic gardens in the Southern Hemisphere. Browse the Riverside Market for last-minute New Zealand souvenirs (Manuka honey, Whittaker's chocolate, Merino wool products, local wine). Return rental car if not already done.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Christchurch International Airport for your departure flight. Allow 2–3 hours before departure for check-in, security, and a final New Zealand flat white at the airport café.
day_by_day.evening: Depart New Zealand — farewell to an extraordinary 13 days on the South Island.

meals.breakfast: Final New Zealand breakfast — treat yourself to a full brunch at a Christchurch café; try Hello Sunday on Fitzgerald Avenue for excellent eggs and coffee
meals.lunch: Light meal at the Riverside Market or Christchurch Airport — try a meat pie, a classic New Zealand farewell snack
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining depending on departure time

day_by_day.notes: Pack any liquid souvenirs (wine, honey, sauces) in checked luggage. New Zealand has strict biosecurity laws — do not attempt to take fresh fruit, meat, or plant material out of the country (or into your next destination). Declare all food items on arrival cards. Leave time to reflect on an incredible trip — 13 days on the South Island covering Queenstown, Fiordland, Mount Cook, and Abel Tasman is a beautifully balanced adventure.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium New Zealand South Island Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Leap from New Zealand's highest bungy platform at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience offers a 8.5-second freefall with breathtaking views of the surrounding Remarkables mountain range. Includes transport from Queenstown and a commemorative certificate.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike one of New Zealand's nine Great Walks, a stunning 32km trail through Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks. Trek past alpine lakes, ancient beech forests, and dramatic mountain passes with panoramic views. A multi-day hike best done over 2-3 days with DOC hut stays along the route.

experiences.name: Hooker Valley Track to Mueller Glacier
experiences.description: Walk one of the most accessible yet spectacular hikes in Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park. This 10km return trail crosses three swing bridges and leads to a glacial lake filled with icebergs at the foot of New Zealand's highest peak. The dramatic alpine scenery is unmatched on the South Island.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo
experiences.description: Paddle through the dramatic fiords of Milford Sound at dawn before the tour boats arrive, gliding past Mitre Peak and cascading waterfalls. Combine with a guided walk on the Milford foreshore track to experience the lush rainforest, resident seals, and dolphins in their natural habitat.

experiences.name: Abel Tasman Coast Track Hiking and Beach Exploration
experiences.description: Hike sections of the famous Abel Tasman Coast Track, weaving through golden beaches, turquoise bays, and native bush. Take a water taxi to drop off and hike back through Torrent Bay and Anchorage, swimming at pristine beaches along the way. A perfect blend of hiking and coastal beauty unique to the South Island.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Queenstown Airport at 13:00. Private luxury transfer arranged to Nevis Valley, Queenstown Boutique Stay. Check in, settle into your suite, and enjoy a welcome champagne with panoramic views of the Remarkables mountain range. Take a leisurely stroll around the boutique property grounds to acclimatise.
day_by_day.evening: Gentle orientation walk into central Queenstown along the lakefront promenade. Explore the vibrant Queenstown waterfront and watch the sunset over Lake Wakatipu from the pier.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in transit
meals.lunch: Light refreshments on arrival at the boutique stay or a casual stop at Vudu Cafe & Larder in central Queenstown for artisan coffee and fresh-baked goods
meals.dinner: Dinner at Amisfield Winery & Bistro — a celebrated farm-to-table restaurant set among vineyards in the Gibbston Valley, offering outstanding Central Otago pinot noir and seasonal tasting menus in a stunning cellar-door setting

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private airport transfer in advance. The boutique stay team should be briefed on your arrival time for a seamless check-in. Keep Day 1 relaxed to recover from long-haul travel. Confirm all activity bookings for the days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Nevis Bungy Jump — the adrenaline highlight of the trip. Transfer via 4WD cable car to the Nevis Bungy platform suspended 134 metres above the Nevis River gorge. Leap from New Zealand's highest bungy platform operated by AJ Hackett. The freefall lasts approximately 8.5 seconds — an iconic, bucket-list experience in one of the world's most dramatic gorges.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Queenstown for a recovery and exploration afternoon. Visit the Queenstown Gardens for a peaceful lakeside walk, then browse the boutique galleries and shops on Beach Street. Optionally book a scenic gondola ride up Bob's Peak for sweeping views over the lake and town.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at Skyline Queenstown's Stratosfare restaurant at the top of the gondola, followed by a premium dinner back in town.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay — eggs benedict, fresh fruit platters, house-made granola and barista coffee
meals.lunch: Post-bungy celebratory lunch at Rata Restaurant in central Queenstown — Chef Josh Emett's flagship offering seasonal New Zealand produce in an elegant heritage building
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Bunker — Queenstown's most intimate fine dining experience, tucked down a laneway, offering an exceptional degustation menu with matched New Zealand wines

day_by_day.notes: The Nevis Bungy Jump requires a minimum weight of 45kg and maximum of 127kg. Wear comfortable, fitted clothing. The activity includes a certificate and professional photos/video package — purchase the media package on the day for lasting memories. Book well in advance as this experience fills quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or private transfer through the stunning Gibbston Valley wine region — known as the 'Valley of the Vines' — stopping for a private cellar-door tasting at Peregrine Wines, one of the region's most architecturally striking wineries. Enjoy a guided tasting of their award-winning Central Otago pinot noirs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the historic Arrowtown — a beautifully preserved 19th-century gold rush town just 20 minutes from Queenstown. Walk the Arrow River Trail through the gorge, visit the Lakes District Museum, and wander the tree-lined main street with its heritage stone buildings and artisan boutiques.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown for a relaxing evening. Enjoy pre-dinner drinks at Minus 5° ICE BAR — a unique experience where the entire bar, including glasses, is made of ice — then dinner at a top Queenstown restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Lunch at The Arrowtown Bakery & Cafe or the acclaimed Provisions of Arrowtown — a charming artisan deli and café serving exceptional seasonal fare
meals.dinner: Dinner at Fishbone Bar & Grill — Queenstown's premier seafood restaurant, celebrated for fresh South Island crayfish, Bluff oysters, and premium New Zealand fish

day_by_day.notes: November is a beautiful time in Arrowtown with autumn foliage lingering and spring wildflowers beginning. The Gibbston Valley cellar-door visits can be pre-arranged as a private guided tasting for a more exclusive experience. Hire a luxury vehicle or arrange a private driver for the day.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early from Queenstown for the drive to the Routeburn Track trailhead (approximately 1.5–2 hours via Glenorchy). Begin the Routeburn Track Great Walk — one of New Zealand's finest alpine hikes. Start at the Routeburn Shelter and hike through lush beech forest, crossing crystal-clear streams to the Routeburn Flats and Routeburn Falls Hut (approximately 4 hours, 9km). The falls cascade dramatically from the alpine plateau above.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking from Routeburn Falls Hut up to the spectacular alpine zone above the treeline. Reach the Harris Saddle viewpoint for panoramic views across the Hollyford Valley and Darran Mountains — one of the most breathtaking vistas in New Zealand. Descend back to the Routeburn Flats for a rest before returning to the trailhead.
day_by_day.evening: Return drive to Queenstown. Arrive early evening. Enjoy a well-deserved soak in a private outdoor hot tub at the boutique stay before dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early packed gourmet breakfast box prepared by the boutique stay — smoked salmon bagels, fresh fruit, energy bars, and a thermos of quality coffee for the trail
meals.lunch: Gourmet trail picnic lunch with premium supplies from Queenstown's Vudu Larder — artisan sandwiches, local cheeses, charcuterie, and fresh fruit packed in an insulated carry bag
meals.dinner: Dinner at Amisfield Winery & Bistro (revisit for a different seasonal menu experience) or try Oishi Japanese Restaurant for exceptional omakase-style dining

day_by_day.notes: The Routeburn Track is a Great Walk requiring advance hut passes from DOC (Department of Conservation) if staying overnight. For a day hike version as described, no pass is needed. Wear high-quality waterproof hiking boots and layered clothing — alpine weather can change rapidly even in November. Trekking poles recommended for the steeper sections. Depart no later than 7:30am to make the most of the day.

day_by_day.morning: Active rest and recovery morning at the boutique stay. Enjoy a slow breakfast, then book an in-room or spa massage treatment to ease hiking muscles. Alternatively, take a gentle yoga session or a peaceful walk around the Queenstown Gardens lakefront.
day_by_day.afternoon: Scenic helicopter flight over the Remarkables, Lake Wakatipu, and the surrounding mountain ranges — a 30-minute luxury scenic flight providing extraordinary aerial perspectives of the South Island landscape. Land back in Queenstown and spend the afternoon exploring the town's luxury boutiques, galleries, and the Queenstown Art Trail.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset lake cruise on Lake Wakatipu aboard the historic TSS Earnslaw steamship — a Queenstown icon. Enjoy champagne on deck as the sun sets behind the Remarkables. Disembark at Walter Peak High Country Farm for an optional gourmet BBQ dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely full breakfast at the boutique stay — eggs any style, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, and a full fruit spread
meals.lunch: Lunch at Sherwood Estate — a celebrated farm-to-table restaurant and organic garden just outside Queenstown, with an exceptional seasonal menu and biodynamic wine list
meals.dinner: Walter Peak High Country Farm Gourmet BBQ Dinner experience aboard the TSS Earnslaw package, featuring premium New Zealand lamb, beef, and seasonal vegetables cooked on the farm's open grill

day_by_day.notes: Book the TSS Earnslaw Gourmet BBQ Dinner package well in advance — it is one of Queenstown's most popular premium evening experiences. The helicopter scenic flight can be booked through Glacier Southern Lakes Helicopters or Over The Top Helicopters, both offering luxury private charter options.

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer from Queenstown to Te Anau (approximately 2 hours). Check in to a premium lodge on the shores of Lake Te Anau. After settling in, take a morning kayak or guided walk along the Te Anau lakefront, enjoying the mirror-still reflections of the Fiordland mountains.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Te Anau Glowworm Caves — a magical underground world accessible only by boat across Lake Te Anau. A guided tour leads through ancient limestone caves adorned with thousands of glowworms illuminating the cavern ceiling like a living galaxy. This is one of Fiordland's most extraordinary natural experiences.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset walk along the Te Anau lakefront with views toward the Murchison Mountains. Enjoy a relaxed evening in Te Anau before the major Milford Sound day tomorrow.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the Queenstown boutique stay before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at The Fat Duck restaurant in Te Anau — a local favourite offering hearty New Zealand cuisine with lake views
meals.dinner: Dinner at Redcliff Cafe & Restaurant in Te Anau — housed in a charming heritage cottage, offering exceptional Fiordland venison, lamb, and fresh fish in an intimate atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: Book the Te Anau Glowworm Caves tour through Real Journeys in advance — evening tours offer a more intimate experience. Accommodation in Te Anau: consider the Fiordland Lodge for a premium wilderness lodge experience with stunning lake and mountain views, or the Te Anau Lodge for boutique heritage accommodation.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Te Anau at dawn for the iconic Milford Sound drive (approximately 2 hours) — one of the world's most scenic road journeys passing through the Avenue of the Disappearing Mountain, the Mirror Lakes, and the Homer Tunnel. Arrive at Milford Sound for the Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo. Begin with a dawn kayaking session on the fiord before the tour boats arrive — paddle beneath the sheer 1,200-metre rock faces of Mitre Peak and Pembroke Glacier, with seals, dolphins, and penguins as potential companions.
day_by_day.afternoon: After kayaking, join the hike component of the combo — explore the Milford foreshore and surrounding rainforest trails, learning about Fiordland's unique ecology from an expert guide. Optionally take a scenic cruise on the fiord aboard a premium small-group vessel for a different perspective of the waterfalls and sheer cliff faces.
day_by_day.evening: Return drive to Te Anau. Arrive early evening. Enjoy a peaceful evening by the lake.

meals.breakfast: Early packed breakfast from the Te Anau lodge — energy-rich foods for the active day ahead
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Milford Sound Lodge Cafe or a gourmet packed lunch prepared by your Te Anau accommodation to enjoy on the fiord foreshore
meals.dinner: Dinner at Fiordland Lodge (if staying there) or return to Redcliff Cafe for their celebrated Fiordland venison and local wine pairing menu

day_by_day.notes: Milford Sound receives extremely high rainfall (up to 8 metres per year) — November can bring rain, which actually enhances the experience as hundreds of temporary waterfalls cascade down the cliff faces. Full waterproof gear is essential. The kayak and hike combo is typically operated by Rosco's Milford Kayaks — book the guided option for the best experience. Depart Te Anau no later than 6:00am to reach Milford for the dawn kayak session.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Te Anau and drive toward Aoraki/Mount Cook (approximately 4.5–5 hours via the Mackenzie Basin). The drive itself is spectacular — passing through Kingston, along the shores of Lake Pukaki with its extraordinary turquoise glacial waters and the first views of Aoraki/Mount Cook on the horizon. Stop at the Church of the Good Shepherd in Tekapo for a brief visit.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Aoraki/Mount Cook Village. Check into the Hermitage Hotel — the iconic luxury lodge at the foot of New Zealand's highest peak. After check-in, take the Kea Point Track (2km return, 1 hour) for immediate up-close views of the Mueller Glacier and the Caroline Face of Aoraki.
day_by_day.evening: Aoraki/Mount Cook is one of the world's premier stargazing locations, sitting within the Aoraki Mackenzie International Dark Sky Reserve. Book a premium private stargazing experience with an expert astronomer guide — observe the Southern Cross, Milky Way, and southern constellations through high-powered telescopes.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the Te Anau lodge before departure
meals.lunch: Stop at the acclaimed Mackenzie Alpine Trust Café in Twizel or the stunning Tekapo Springs Café overlooking Lake Tekapo
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Hermitage Hotel's Panorama Restaurant — offering a premium à la carte menu with floor-to-ceiling windows framing Aoraki/Mount Cook, paired with Marlborough and Central Otago wines

day_by_day.notes: Book the Hermitage Hotel well in advance — it is the only luxury accommodation option within the national park. The stargazing experience can be arranged through Earth & Sky Ltd, which operates from the Mount John Observatory area. November offers long daylight hours but clear nights can still be spectacular. The drive along Lake Pukaki is unmissable — allow time for photography stops.

day_by_day.morning: Hooker Valley Track to Mueller Glacier — one of the South Island's most spectacular and accessible hikes. Begin at the White Horse Hill Campground and follow the Hooker Valley Track (10km return, 3–4 hours) through three swing bridges over glacial rivers, past the Mueller Lake terminal moraine with floating icebergs, and on to the Hooker Lake viewpoint with Aoraki/Mount Cook towering directly above. The scale and drama of this landscape is extraordinary.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return from the Hooker Valley Track. Enjoy a relaxing afternoon at the Hermitage Hotel. Book a scenic helicopter flight over the Tasman Glacier and Aoraki/Mount Cook — a 40-minute premium alpine flight with a glacier landing, offering perspectives of the mountain that are otherwise impossible to access.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the Hermitage. Enjoy the hotel's lounge bar with a glass of Central Otago pinot noir while watching alpenglow paint the summit of Aoraki in shades of pink and gold.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the Hermitage Hotel's dining room before the hike
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch from the Hermitage — quality sandwiches, fruit, chocolate, and a thermos of hot soup for the alpine conditions
meals.dinner: Dinner at the Hermitage Hotel's Panorama Restaurant — three-course premium dinner featuring South Island lamb rack, fresh Canterbury salmon, and a selection of New Zealand artisan cheeses

day_by_day.notes: The Hooker Valley Track is well-formed and suitable for all fitness levels, but alpine conditions can change rapidly — carry a waterproof jacket regardless of morning weather. The helicopter glacier landing experience can be booked through The Helicopter Line, which operates from the Glentanner airfield near the village. This is one of the most memorable experiences available in New Zealand — highly recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Aoraki/Mount Cook and drive north toward Nelson/Marlborough region (approximately 5–6 hours to Nelson). The drive passes through the golden Mackenzie Basin, the historic town of Fairlie, and the beautiful Hurunui district. Stop at Hamner Springs for a 1-hour soak in the premium Alpine Spa thermal pools.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue driving to Nelson, arriving mid-afternoon. Check into a premium boutique hotel in Nelson — consider the Trailways Hotel Nelson or a luxury lodge in the nearby Tasman region. Explore Nelson's vibrant arts precinct, including the World of WearableArt & Classic Cars Museum, and the Suter Art Gallery.
day_by_day.evening: Nelson is New Zealand's sunniest city and a celebrated food and wine destination. Explore the central city, visit the Saturday Farmers Market (if timing aligns), and enjoy a relaxed first evening in the region.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the Hermitage Hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch at Hanmer Springs' Powerhouse Café or a stop at a quality café in Christchurch if passing through
meals.dinner: Dinner at The Boat Shed Café in Nelson — an iconic waterfront restaurant built over the water on stilts, renowned for exceptional fresh seafood, including Nelson scallops, green-lipped mussels, and locally caught fish

day_by_day.notes: This is a long driving day — consider breaking the journey with meaningful stops rather than rushing. Alternatively, arrange a scenic flight from Mount Cook to Nelson to save time and experience the South Island from the air. Nelson is the gateway to the Abel Tasman National Park, which features prominently in the coming days.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Nelson early for the Abel Tasman Coast Track Hiking and Beach Exploration experience. Drive to Marahau (approximately 1 hour from Nelson) — the southern gateway to Abel Tasman National Park. Begin hiking the Abel Tasman Coast Track, weaving through golden-sand beaches, turquoise bays, and regenerating native forest. The section from Marahau to Bark Bay (approximately 15km) is among the most beautiful coastal walking in the world.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking through the park's signature golden-sand coves — stopping at Anchorage Beach, Te Pukatea Bay, and Torrent Bay. The track winds through lush coastal forest with stunning views across Tasman Bay. Optionally arrange a water taxi to return from a further point in the park, allowing a one-way hike deeper into the park.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Nelson via water taxi and road transfer. Arrive early evening. Enjoy a sunset drink at a Nelson waterfront bar overlooking the harbour.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the Nelson hotel before departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet packed picnic lunch enjoyed on one of the Abel Tasman's pristine golden beaches — premium supplies arranged by your accommodation including local cheeses, artisan bread, charcuterie, and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hopgoods & Co in Nelson — one of the South Island's finest restaurants, offering a seasonally driven menu with exceptional local produce, craft beers, and an outstanding New Zealand wine list

day_by_day.notes: November is an ideal time for Abel Tasman — warm temperatures, long daylight hours, and the park is not yet at peak summer capacity. Book the water taxi return with Abel Tasman Aqua Taxi in advance. Wear sun protection — the coastal track offers little shade on the beach sections. The track is well-formed but involves some tidal crossings — check tide tables before departure.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure in Nelson. Visit the Nelson Saturday Farmers Market at Montgomery Square (one of New Zealand's finest) for local produce, artisan foods, and crafts. Explore the Nelson Arts District — visit local galleries, the Nelson Provincial Museum, and the stunning Cathedral of Christ Church on the hill.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a private guided tour of the Waimea Plains wine region — Nelson produces exceptional sauvignon blanc, chardonnay, and pinot noir. Visit two or three premium boutique wineries including Neudorf Vineyards (one of New Zealand's most acclaimed small wineries) and Seifried Estate for private cellar-door tastings with the winemakers.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Nelson — enjoy a sunset walk along the Nelson waterfront, then a special farewell dinner at one of the region's finest restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely breakfast at the Nelson hotel or at a local café — try Lambretta's Café Bar for excellent coffee and breakfast in a vibrant atmosphere
meals.lunch: Lunch at Neudorf Vineyards' cellar door during the wine tour — a beautifully curated cheese and charcuterie platter matched with their estate wines
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Hopgoods & Co or the acclaimed Arbour Restaurant in Blenheim (a short drive or taxi) — a garden-to-table fine dining experience in a stunning setting with an extraordinary Marlborough wine list

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange the private winery tour through a Nelson-based luxury tour operator such as Waimea Estates or a private guide. Neudorf Vineyards is particularly special — their chardonnay is considered among New Zealand's finest. The drive through the Waimea Plains in November is beautiful with vineyards in full leaf.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Nelson. Enjoy a leisurely farewell breakfast at the hotel. Take a final walk along the Nelson waterfront or up to the Centre of New Zealand viewpoint — a short 30-minute walk to the geographic centre of the country, offering panoramic views over Nelson, Tasman Bay, and the Richmond Ranges.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Nelson Airport for departure flights. Alternatively, if flying via Christchurch or Auckland, arrange a scenic flight over the Marlborough Sounds — an extraordinary final aerial perspective of the South Island's coastline, inlets, and mountain ranges.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from New Zealand. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days across the South Island — from the bungee platforms of Queenstown to the fiords of Milford Sound, the glaciers of Aoraki, and the golden beaches of Abel Tasman.

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet breakfast at the Nelson hotel — make it a celebration with eggs benedict, smoked salmon, fresh pastries, and a glass of Marlborough sparkling wine
meals.lunch: Light lunch at Nelson Airport or a final stop at a Nelson café — try the Organic Organics Café for healthy, locally sourced farewell bites
meals.dinner: In-flight dining or airport lounge dining depending on departure time and connection

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2 hours before departure for airport check-in and security. Confirm all onward flight connections well in advance — Nelson Airport (NSN) operates domestic flights to Auckland (AKL) and Wellington (WLG) with connections to international services. Consider purchasing premium New Zealand souvenirs — Marlborough wine, Nelson sea salt, Whittaker's chocolate, and New Zealand merino wool products make excellent gifts. Ensure all adventure activity media packages (bungy photos/videos, helicopter footage) are downloaded and backed up before departure.
